subject: maths
title: Addition and Subtraction within 20
seo_title: Year 1 Addition and Subtraction within 20 Worksheets: Number Bonds, Doubles and Make Ten
standard_text: Add and subtract numbers within 20, using physical and virtual materials, part-part-whole knowledge to 10 and a variety of calculation strategies
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets on addition and subtraction within 20, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M1N04): adding with pictures and ten frames, number bonds to 10, counting on and back on a number line, doubles, make ten, taking away and finding the difference. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Add: count on. Take away: count back. Know your bonds to 10.
key_sub: 9 + 3: say 9, then count 10, 11, 12. 8 + 6: fill a ten first, so 10 + 4 = 14. 13 − 4: go back to 10, then 1 more to 9.
body_html:
Add: put together and count on

Adding means putting groups together. The sign is +. Say “add” or “plus”.

You can count all of them. It is faster to start at the bigger number and count on.

Count on

9 + 3 = ?

Say 9. Then count 3 more: 10, 11, 12.

Answer: 12

Number bonds to 10

Two parts make a whole. These pairs make 10. Learn them well. They help with bigger numbers.

Number bond to 10Turned around
1 + 99 + 1
2 + 88 + 2
3 + 77 + 3
4 + 66 + 4
5 + 55 + 5 is a double

Count back on a number line

Subtracting means taking away. The sign is −. Say “take away” or “minus”. On a number line, start at the first number and jump back.

Doubles and make ten

A double adds a number to itself: 6 + 6 = 12. A near double is 1 more: 6 + 7 = 13.

To make ten, fill a ten frame first. Then add what is left.

Take away or find the difference

Take away: cross some out and count what is left.

Find the difference: line up two groups. Count the extra ones. Or count up from the smaller number.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the start number: 9 + 3 → “9, 10, 11”, so 11Say 9, then count 3 more: 10, 11, 12. 9 + 3 = 12
Adding when you should take away: 12 − 5 = 17Look at the sign. Words like “left” and “fewer” mean subtract
Taking the small digit from the big one: 12 − 5 = 13Go back to 10 first: 12 − 2 = 10, then 10 − 3 = 7
Writing 10 + 4 as 10410 + 4 is 1 ten and 4 ones. That is 14
Adding to find the difference: 9 and 6 → 15Difference means how many more. 9 − 6 = 3

faq.q: What addition and subtraction does Year 1 learn in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 1 students add and subtract numbers within 20 (AC9M1N04). They use objects, ten frames, part-part-whole knowledge to 10 and strategies such as counting on, counting back, doubles and making ten.
They are the pairs of numbers that make 10: 1 + 9, 2 + 8, 3 + 7, 4 + 6 and 5 + 5, and the same pairs turned around. Many Australian classrooms call them “friends of ten” or “rainbow facts”.

faq.q: What is the make ten strategy?
faq.a: Fill up a ten first, then add the rest. For 8 + 6, take 2 from the 6 to make 10, so 8 + 6 = 10 + 4 = 14.

faq.q: How can I help my Year 1 child with adding and subtracting at home?
faq.a: Use 10 to 20 small objects, a ten frame or a dice game for a few minutes a day. Ask questions like “I have 6. How many more make 10?” and “How many more does Jack have than Mia?”

items.q:

10 − 6 = ?
items.e: 6 + 4 = 10. Take away the part 6. The part 4 is left. 10 − 6 = 4.

items.q:

items.q: Which is not a number bond to 10?
items.e: 4 + 5 = 9, not 10. So 4 + 5 is not a number bond to 10. The others all make 10.

sets.title: Subtract: take away and find the difference

items.q: Zara has 8 balloons at her party. 3 balloons pop. How many balloons are left?
items.e: Pop means gone, so take away. Start at 8. Count back 3: 7, 6, 5. Do not count the 8. 8 − 3 = 5.

items.q: The class has 11 apples for recess. The students eat 3. How many apples are left?
items.e: Eaten apples are gone, so take away. Go back to 10 first: 11 − 1 = 10. Then take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.

items.q: Mum bakes 12 Anzac biscuits. The family eats 4. How many biscuits are left?
items.e: Eaten biscuits are gone, so take away. Go back to 10 first: 12 − 2 = 10. Then take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.

items.q: 15 fish swim in a rock pool. 6 fish swim away. How many fish are left?
items.e: Some swim away, so take away. Go back to 10 first: 15 − 5 = 10. Then take away 1 more: 10 − 1 = 9.

items.q: There are 17 balls in the sport shed. Class 1B takes 5 to the oval. How many balls are left in the shed?
items.e: Some are taken, so take away. Cross out 5. Count the ones with no cross: 12. 17 − 5 = 12.

items.q: 13 children are in the pool at swimming lessons. 4 get out. How many are still in the pool?
items.e: Getting out means take away. Go back to 10 first: 13 − 3 = 10. Then take away 1 more: 10 − 1 = 9.
Match them up. 6 of Mia’s stickers have a partner. 3 do not. The difference is 3. 9 − 6 = 3.

items.q: Jack has 12 toy cars. Noah has 8. How many more toy cars does Jack have?
items.e: Match them up. 8 of Jack’s toy cars have a partner. 4 do not. The difference is 4. 12 − 8 = 4.

items.q: Isla picks 13 flowers. Ruby picks 7. How many fewer flowers does Ruby pick?
items.e: Match them up. 7 of Isla’s flowers have a partner. 6 do not. The difference is 6. 13 − 7 = 6.

items.q: Kai has a row of 15 blocks. Sienna has a row of 10. How many more blocks does Kai have?
items.e: Match them up. 10 of Kai’s blocks have a partner. 5 do not. The difference is 5. 15 − 10 = 5.

items.q:
What is the difference between 14 and 9?
Count up from 9 to 14.
items.e: Count up from 9: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. That is 5 jumps. 14 − 9 = 5.

items.q:
What is the difference between 16 and 12?
Count up from 12 to 16.
items.e: Count up from 12: 13, 14, 15, 16. That is 4 jumps. 16 − 12 = 4.

items.q: There are 20 sausages at the school sausage sizzle. 6 are sold. How many sausages are left?
items.e: Sold sausages are gone, so take away. 20 is 10 and 10. 10 − 6 = 4. 10 and 4 is 14. 20 − 6 = 14.

items.q: Grace has $15. She spends $6 on a book. How much money does she have left?
items.e: Spending means take away. Go back to 10 first: 15 − 5 = 10. Then take away 1 more: 10 − 1 = 9.

items.q: Noah is 7. His sister Matilda is 12. How many years older is Matilda?
items.e: Find the difference. Count up from 7 to 12: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. That is 5 years. 12 − 7 = 5.

items.q: 16 students are in the class. 4 go to the library. Which number sentence shows how many are left?
items.e: 4 students go, so take them away from 16. 16 − 4 = 12.

items.q: Liam has 11 marbles. Chloe has 18 marbles. How many more marbles does Chloe have?
items.e: Find the difference. Count up from 11 to 18: 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18. That is 7 more.

items.q: At the beach, 19 children swim between the flags. 7 get out. How many are still swimming?
items.e: Getting out means take away. 19 is 10 and 9. 9 − 7 = 2. 10 and 2 is 12. 19 − 7 = 12.

items.q: Some kangaroos are in a paddock. 5 hop away. Now 8 are left. How many kangaroos were there at the start?
items.e: Put back the 5 that hopped away: 8 + 5 = 13. Check: 13 − 5 = 8. (8 − 5 = 3 is the wrong way.)

items.q: Charlotte has 14 shells. William has 9 shells. What is the difference?
